findings.title: Direct requests.get() call violates ADR-006 HTTP client standard
findings.explanation: ADR-006 requires all outbound HTTP calls to use make_client() which provides standardized timeouts (3s connect, 10s read), 2 retries with jittered backoff on connect errors and 502/503/504, request-id propagation, and metrics. Direct requests.get() bypasses this infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Replace requests.get() with a client built using make_client('card_network_statuspage') and store it in module-level _statuspage_client, following the pattern of _client on line 8. Remove the requests import.

findings.title: Service layer raises HTTPException instead of domain error
findings.explanation: Services must raise domain errors from app.errors because they're called from multiple contexts (API, workers, jobs, CLI) where HTTP semantics don't apply. HTTPException is only valid in API handlers.
findings.recommendation: Define a domain error in app/errors.py (e.g., InvalidStatusIndicator or NetworkStatusUnavailable) and raise that instead. Let the API layer map it to HTTP 502 if needed.

findings.title: Dangerous fallback: defaulting to 'up' status when status page is unreachable
findings.explanation: Lines 22-23 catch all exceptions from status_page_indicator() and default indicator to 'none', which maps to 'up' status. If the status page is unreachable or returns malformed data, the system incorrectly reports the network as operational.
findings.recommendation: Either propagate the exception (safest: fail if both APIs are down) or return a distinct 'unknown' status that callers can handle appropriately. Don't claim 'up' when you cannot verify status.

findings.title: Bare except Exception hides unexpected errors
findings.explanation: Catching Exception is too broad and will silently swallow unexpected errors like KeyError (missing 'status' key), connection timeouts, DNS failures, etc. This makes debugging harder and masks real problems.
findings.recommendation: Catch specific exceptions (httpx.HTTPError, httpx.TimeoutException, KeyError) or remove the fallback entirely and let the exception propagate. At minimum, log the exception details before defaulting.

findings.title: requests library import suggests missing dependency declaration
findings.explanation: M7 notes that 'requests library not in declared dependencies' as part of enforcing ADR-006's make_client pattern. This import suggests either undeclared dependency or violation of the convention to use only httpx via make_client.
findings.recommendation: Remove requests import entirely and use make_client() which returns httpx.Client. If requests is not in requirements.txt, this code will fail in production.

findings.title: Missing timeout on status API call (compare with status page)
findings.explanation: The status_page_indicator() explicitly sets timeout=5 on line 17, but network_status() relies on _client's default timeouts. While make_client provides 3s connect/10s read, the inconsistency suggests different intent.
findings.recommendation: Document why different timeout strategies are appropriate for the two endpoints, or unify the approach. The API call uses make_client's retry logic while the page doesn't, which may be intentional.
